**Greg Vanney** (born June 11, 1974) is an American [soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") manager and former professional player who is the head coach of the [LA Galaxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LA_Galaxy "LA Galaxy") in [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer").
A [defender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defender_\(association_football\) "Defender \(association football\)") and one of MLS's original players, Vanney spent 10 seasons in the league and another three-and-a-half in the French First Division playing for [Sporting Club de Bastia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Bastia "SC Bastia") between 2002 and 2005. He also earned 36 [caps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cap_\(sports\) "Cap \(sports\)"), scoring one goal, with the [U.S. national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team") between 1996 and 2006.
In 2017, as coach of [Toronto FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_FC "Toronto FC"), Vanney won the [domestic treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_treble "Domestic treble") by lifting the [MLS Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLS_Cup_2017 "MLS Cup 2017"), [Supporters' Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supporters'_Shield "Supporters' Shield") and the [Canadian Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Canadian_Championship "2017 Canadian Championship"), also being named [MLS Coach of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigi_Schmid_Coach_of_the_Year_Award "Sigi Schmid Coach of the Year Award"). He won a second MLS Cup as coach of the LA Galaxy in [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLS_Cup_2024 "MLS Cup 2024").
## Playing career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Playing career")]
### High school and college
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: High school and college")]
Vanney played soccer for [Marcos de Niza High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_de_Niza_High_School "Marcos de Niza High School") in Tempe, Arizona, and led the team to three consecutive state championship titles in 1990, 1991, and 1992. Vanney holds the school record for most assists by one player in a season with 13 for the 1990–1991 season, and also holds the school record for most goals by one player in a single season with 33 goals for the 1991–1992 season. He was also named the 5A player of the year for the 1991–1992 season, [Gatorade Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gatorade_Player_of_the_Year "Gatorade Player of the Year"), [NSCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSCAA "NSCAA") and Parade All-America in 1992. Greg Vanney played [college soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_soccer_in_the_United_States "College soccer in the United States") for [Florida International University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_International_University "Florida International University") in 1992, and for [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA "UCLA") from 1993 to 1995. In 1995, Vanney was named All-America honorable mention and finished his senior season with 8 goals and 10 assists.
### Professional
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Professional")]
Vanney was drafted 17th overall in the [1996 MLS College Draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_MLS_College_Draft "1996 MLS College Draft") by the [Los Angeles Galaxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Galaxy "Los Angeles Galaxy"). The team sent him on loan to the [Sacramento Scorpions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Scorpions "Sacramento Scorpions") of [USISL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USISL "USISL") for three games at the beginning of the season where he netted three goals in three games including two game winners.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-2) Vanney played for the Galaxy for six years, from 1996 to 2001, and was consistently one of the best defenders in MLS, leading the Galaxy to three [MLS Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLS_Cup "MLS Cup") Finals and two [CONCACAF Champion's Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONCACAF_Champions_League "CONCACAF Champions League") Finals. He was named to the [MLS Best XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLS_Best_XI "MLS Best XI") in both 2000 and 2001, and an MLS All-Star in 2001. After the 2001 MLS season, Vanney transferred to the French First Division club [SC Bastia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Bastia "SC Bastia"). In the first six months with Bastia, Vanney helped lead the French club to its first appearance in the [Coupe de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coupe_de_France "Coupe de France") Final in over 20 years. He left the club in 2005, coming back to MLS and signing with [FC Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dallas "FC Dallas"). After two seasons with the Hoops, and two All-Star selections, Vanney was traded to [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rapids "Colorado Rapids") on January 12, 2007. On June 29, 2007, he was traded from the Rapids to [D.C. United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.C._United "D.C. United").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-mlsnet-3) On February 15, 2008, the rights for Vanney were transferred to his first club, the [Los Angeles Galaxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Galaxy "Los Angeles Galaxy"). Vanney announced his retirement from the professional game on October 26, 2008; his last game against his former club [FC Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dallas "FC Dallas").
### International
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: International")]
Vanney also spent 11 years as a member of the [United States national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team"), debuting December 21, 1996 against [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala_national_football_team "Guatemala national football team"), and played 36 games and scored one goal (September 2005). Vanney participated in three [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") qualifying cycles for the United States (1998, 2002 and 2006). He was originally named as an alternate for the [2002 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup") but initially replaced the injured Chris Armas on the roster after the midfielder picked up an ACL injury in a warm-up friendly against Uruguay on May 12, 2002. Vanney was himself injured in the next warm-up friendly on May 16, 2002, against [Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_national_football_team "Jamaica national football team") and was replaced on the roster by [Steve Cherundolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Cherundolo "Steve Cherundolo"). Vanney also was a member of the 2005 CONCACAF Gold Cup Championship team and was featured in the early part of [2006 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup") qualifying for the United States.
## Coaching career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Coaching career")]
### Early career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Early career")]
Vanney has more than 15 years experience in youth soccer: coaching, directing and consulting. He holds a USSF "A" Coaching License and has been actively involved with the U.S. Soccer Development Academy as a scout and other programming.
Vanney co-founded Arizona Futbol Club, a youth soccer club, in 1997 using a business plan Vanney started as a class assignment while attending UCLA. The club was later merged into [Sereno Soccer Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sereno_Soccer_Club?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sereno Soccer Club \(page does not exist\)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-5)
Vanney was a member of the U.S. Soccer Education Staff that traveled to Spain in March 2010.
Vanney was an Academy Director for [Real Salt Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Salt_Lake "Real Salt Lake") from 2008 to 2011.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-Ryan_Nelsen_fired_as_Toronto_FC_coach-6) Vanney and his staff, with the support of Grande Sports World and [Real Salt Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Salt_Lake "Real Salt Lake"), established the first [MLS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") Residential Academy in the United States in fewer than 8 months. The U-18 and U-16 boys teams began play in Fall 2010.
Greg Vanney moved back to Arizona in 2008. For some time, he held two titles: (1.) Director of Soccer Operations at Grande Sports World in [Casa Grande, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Grande,_Arizona "Casa Grande, Arizona") and (2.) Director of the [Real Salt Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Salt_Lake "Real Salt Lake")-Arizona Youth Academy. As Director of Soccer Operations, Vanney oversaw program and event development at the Grande Sports World facility featuring 8 professional quality fields; state-of-the-art 58,000 sq ft (5,400 m2) performance center with 4 stadium quality locker rooms; 10,000 sq ft (930 m2) weight room, physical therapy and 16 classrooms. In the first year, Vanney has help attract four professional teams ([Real Salt Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Salt_Lake "Real Salt Lake"), [Seattle Sounders FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Sounders_FC "Seattle Sounders FC"), [Colorado Rapids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rapids "Colorado Rapids"), and [Vancouver Whitecaps FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Whitecaps_FC "Vancouver Whitecaps FC")) to the facility to host their preseason camps.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
In January 2011, Vanney joined [Chivas USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chivas_USA "Chivas USA") as an assistant coach.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-Ryan_Nelsen_fired_as_Toronto_FC_coach-6)
### Toronto FC
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Toronto FC")]

— [[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-Toronto_FC_fires_coaches,_Jermain_Defoe_might_go-7)
Vanney got his first head coaching job in [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") when he became the ninth head coach for [Toronto FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_FC "Toronto FC") after [Ryan Nelsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Nelsen "Ryan Nelsen") was dismissed on August 31, 2014, with 10 games remaining in the [2014 regular season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Toronto_FC_season "2014 Toronto FC season").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-Toronto_FC_fires_coaches,_Jermain_Defoe_might_go-7) He inherited a 9–9–6 record.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-Toronto_FC_fires_coaches,_Jermain_Defoe_might_go-7) In his debut match, Toronto lost 1–0 to the [Philadelphia Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Union "Philadelphia Union").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-8) His first win came in a match that finished 3–0 against [Chivas USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chivas_USA "Chivas USA").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-9) He finished off the [2014 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Toronto_FC_season "2014 Toronto FC season") in seventh place in the Eastern Conference[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-2014_league_table-10) with a record of two wins, six losses and two ties.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-2014_season-11)
Toronto were eliminated from the [Canadian Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Canadian_Championship "2015 Canadian Championship") during the [2015 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Toronto_FC_season "2015 Toronto FC season"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-Canadian_Championship_2015-12) although they qualified for the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_MLS_Cup_Playoffs "2015 MLS Cup Playoffs") for the first time that season, after finishing sixth in the Eastern Conference.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-2015_league_table-13) The club's [rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/401_Derby "401 Derby") [Montreal Impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CF_Montr%C3%A9al "CF Montréal") eliminated Toronto in the knockout round.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-2015_playoffs-14)
During the [2016 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Toronto_FC_season "2016 Toronto FC season"), Toronto won the [Canadian Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Canadian_Championship "2016 Canadian Championship")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-Canadian_Championship_2016-15) and qualified for the playoffs after finishing in third place in the Eastern Conference.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-2016_league_table-16) They got to the [MLS Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLS_Cup_2016 "MLS Cup 2016")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-2016_playoffs-17) where they lost in shoot-out 5–4 to [Seattle Sounders FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Sounders_FC "Seattle Sounders FC") following a goalless draw after extra-time.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-18)
The arrival of Spanish playmaker [Victor Vázquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%ADctor_V%C3%A1zquez_Solsona "Víctor Vázquez Solsona") in midfield at the beginning of the 2017 season saw less responsibility placed on the club's star forward [Sebastian Giovinco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Giovinco "Sebastian Giovinco") and captain [Michael Bradley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bradley_\(soccer\) "Michael Bradley \(soccer\)") to create Toronto's goalscoring opportunities, and this in turn freed up the Italian, enabling him to focus more on his attacking game; furthermore, Greg Vanney's switch in tactics from a [4–4–2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_\(association_football\)#4.E2.80.934.E2.80.932 "Formation \(association football\)") [diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_\(association_football\)#4.E2.80.934.E2.80.932_diamond_or_4.E2.80.931.E2.80.932.E2.80.931.E2.80.932 "Formation \(association football\)") to a [3–5–2 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_\(association_football\)#3.E2.80.935.E2.80.932 "Formation \(association football\)") benefitted Giovinco's and [Jozy Altidore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jozy_Altidore "Jozy Altidore")'s attacking partnership: by playing closer together, and with Vázquez now supporting them as the team's main creator, the attacking duo began to demonstrate a deeper understanding and an increased awareness of each other's movements, which improved their link-up play, and saw an increase in Altidore's goalscoring output throughout the season.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-big_read-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-magic-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-21) On June 27, Toronto defeated Montreal 2–1 at home in the second leg of the [2017 Canadian Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Canadian_Championship "2017 Canadian Championship") final to capture the title for the second consecutive season, edging Montreal 3–2 on aggregate.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-mem-22) On September 30, 2017, Toronto FC captured the [Supporters' Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supporters'_Shield "Supporters' Shield") with a 4–2 home win over [New York Red Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Red_Bulls "New York Red Bulls"), to clinch top of the league with the most points [that season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Major_League_Soccer_season "2017 Major League Soccer season").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-23) On November 27, 2017, Vanney won the [MLS Coach of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLS_Coach_of_the_Year "MLS Coach of the Year") award.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-24) On December 9, 2017, Vanney led Toronto FC to [MLS Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_MLS_Cup "2017 MLS Cup") victory in a 2–0 victory against Seattle.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-mlscupwin-25) Greg Vanney was also named [CONCACAF Coach of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONCACAF_Awards "CONCACAF Awards").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-26)
Following an early round play-off elimination, Vanney resigned as coach of Toronto FC on December 1, 2020.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-27)
### LA Galaxy
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greg_Vanney&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: LA Galaxy")]
In January 2021, Vanney was named as head coach of the [LA Galaxy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LA_Galaxy "LA Galaxy"), his former club, where he played for seven seasons.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Vanney#cite_note-28)
After narrowly missing the playoffs in 2021, Vanney's Galaxy finished fourth in the Western Conference (ninth overall) in the 2022 season, the highest positions for the club since 2016. LA beat Nashville 1–0 in the first round, but fell to rivals [Los Angeles FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_FC "Los Angeles FC") 3–2 in the conference semifinals.
In 2024, Vanney led the Galaxy to its highest points total since 1998 (64, on par with the 2014 MLS Cup-winning side). The Galaxy would win MLS Cup against the [New York Red Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Red_Bulls "New York Red Bulls"), 2-1, thus giving Vanney his second MLS Cup as a coach and the Galaxy's first in exactly 10 years.
